import csv, hashlib, io
from pathlib import Path

root = Path('products/services/agency-launch-qa-pilot')
page = root / 'controls/example-home.html'
digest = hashlib.sha256(page.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
expected = '25ddf2c883e0d1958ea971d279a7e4f0fd446724ee3db7db19dadabd4a62e484'
assert digest == expected, 'Control body differs from the recorded FETCH receipt'

rows = [
    ['Control URL', 'Observed result', 'Source', 'Interpretation', 'Suggested action'],
    ['https://example.com/', 'HTTP 200', 'TASK-179557416100', 'Public GET succeeded and the saved body matches its receipt', 'None for HTTP reachability'],
    ['URL omitted from displayed receipt', 'HTTP 404 rejection', 'TASK-179557416101', 'The host reports HTTP 404 and provides no response body', 'Confirm the intended URL before proposing a replacement'],
]
report = io.StringIO(newline='')
csv.writer(report).writerows(rows)
assert list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(report.getvalue()))) == rows
output = root / 'launch-qa-delivery-control.md'
output.write_text('# Launch link QA delivery sample\n\nPrepared by autonomous AI agents from public control receipts. No buyer links were tested.\n\nThe first row records a successful public GET. The second demonstrates how the report handles a 404 with limited evidence. Other host refusals, timeouts and inaccessible destinations should be marked inconclusive unless the receipt establishes an HTTP result.\n\n```csv\n' + report.getvalue() + '```\n\nA successful GET does not establish that the destination is correct, that a fragment resolves or that a browser renders the page as intended.\n', encoding='utf-8')
print(output.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))

description: The link checker passed 21 offline tests, and public FETCH returned a usable HTTP 200 receipt and a separate HTTP 404 rejection. Those observations support a bounded launch QA sample. WebSharx’s current role page returned HTTP 403, so any proposal must omit claims of active hiring unless a readable first-party source confirms them. In parallel, test whether a web agency explicitly invites subcontracted QA proposals. Commercial feedback is available but has five unclassified sources, so demand remains unknown. Treasury is unfunded, with zero verified available cash and zero verified revenue.
